controller_policy_change.rationale: User explicitly released the GPU and requested actual testing. CPU heap size and CPU compiler presence alone were removed as GPU-exclusion signals. Mapped Python below 512MiB is recorded as unconfirmed library presence; this heuristic does not establish GPU exclusivity.

limits: One mirrored cross-process/load window with six measured requests per arm; block drift and ambient CPU work prevent reliable causal or sustained-gain claims.
Protocol qualification means a completed guarded comparison, not numerical or performance production admission; no default or dispatch adoption follows.
All earlier completed calls are retained separately and excluded from final-window summaries; failed/interrupted attempts are not clean timing evidence.
One-second process metadata sampling can miss short GPU activity. Vanished Python does not prove GPU inactivity; no exclusive-GPU or zero-CPU claim.
The mapped-Python 512MiB RSS threshold is a heuristic. Genuine lightweight GPU activity can pass it; low-RSS GPU-library mappings are unconfirmed and remain an ambient confounder.
The controller's lightweight library imports wording is a heuristic label only. Mappings plus RSS do not prove import-only or CPU-only behavior, or GPU inactivity.
The identified Planetable script is a generic dispatcher and was not whitelisted by name, path or hash.
GPU clock/thermal telemetry was not captured. Worker readiness may expose no precision metadata; precision is bound through source and binary seals.
Synthetic byte identity and one fixed seeded continuation do not establish full-vocabulary equality, broader answer quality or cross-engine equivalence.
